title: SHM Velocity
prompt: A particle in simple harmonic motion has displacement x(t) = 3*sin(2*t). Find its velocity v(t) = dx/dt.
hint: chain rule: d/dt[sin(ω t)] = ω·cos(ω t)
recap:
Velocity is the time-derivative of displacement. For SHM x(t) = A·sin(ω t), the chain rule gives v(t) = A·ω·cos(ω t): the speed is greatest (A·ω) as the particle passes through equilibrium and zero at the turning points.

Example — x(t) = 3·sin(2t): v(t) = 6·cos(2t); peak speed 6 at t = 0.

Energy check: max KE = (1/2)m(Aω)² equals the max PE = (1/2)kA² since k = mω². Reference: Kleppner & Kolenkow, An Introduction to Mechanics, ch. 11.
